::: info INSERT-NAMES-COLUMNS
**Name the columns in every INSERT**

Write every INSERT with its column list: INSERT INTO marks (body, at) VALUES (?, ?), never INSERT INTO marks VALUES (?, ?).

**Why.** A table that declares no primary key is given one, \_dai\_id, as its first column, so every copy names its rows alike. SELECT \* shows it, and an INSERT that relies on column order has one value too few and fails.

<small>Applies to every shape · checked by the lint (`positional-insert`) · [INSERT-NAMES-COLUMNS in Constraints](/docs/constraints#INSERT-NAMES-COLUMNS)</small>
:::
